literal_meaning: মাঠে সার দেওয়া (field mein saar dewa - fertilizing in the field)
similar_in_english: Doing one's business in the open
example_sentences_in_bangla: গ্রামে অনেকেই এখনও মাঠে সারা করে।
সকালে উঠে সে মাঠে সারা করতে গেল।
example_sentences_in_english: In the village, many people still go to the field to do their business.
He went to the field to relieve himself in the morning.
history: This idiom reflects traditional rural Bengali practices where open defecation in fields was common due to limited sanitation facilities, especially in the mornings when people would go to the fields.
note: A polite euphemism used in rural contexts to refer to defecation, highlighting cultural norms around privacy and agriculture.
